usage: This is the standard, polite way to say please in Modern Standard Arabic when making a request. It is highly versatile, used in formal writing, news broadcasts, and polite speech across the Arab world. The ending pronoun must change depending on the gender and number of the people being addressed.

variants.label: to a man
variants.note: Use when addressing a single male.

variants.label: to a woman
variants.note: Use when addressing a single female.

variants.label: to a group
variants.note: Use when addressing a group of three or more people, or a mixed group.

variants.label: I beg you
variants.note: Use for a stronger, more emotional plea rather than a simple polite request.

variants.label: if you permit
variants.note: Another very common polite request marker, slightly less formal than min fadlika.
